newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bank Melbourne shares up with merger hopes.
newsitem.headline: Bank Melbourne shares up with merger hopes.

text.p: Shares in Australia's Bank of Melbourne Ltd, target of an agreed takeover by Westpac Banking Corp, firmed on Friday as doubters began to question a rumour that the deal was doomed.

The bank's shares rallied to A$9.15 at 0135 GMT (11.35 a.m.), up 20 cents on Thursday's close. The shares had fallen on Thursday on a rumour Australia's anti-monopolies watchdog would scupper the merger.
Westpac in April bid A$9.75 per share for Bank of Melbourne, valuing the regional bank at about A$1.4 billion.
The ACCC has delayed making a decision on the deal.
But Fels said on Friday this reflected ongoing inquiries into the merger's effect on competition for transaction accounts, like cheque and savings accounts, and credit cards.
The ACCC has no concerns on the merger's effect on competition for home borrowers, he said.
